# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="push") — the large button
    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The previous gesture used a symbol outside the permitted alphabet, so it was not sent. I will resend the request using only valid gestures. I ask Mute for the manual and for relayed visual observations, while signaling Deaf to report the bomb’s visible features.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please tell me the manual's exact defusal instructions, and relay the Deaf monkey's readings of the display, light, button, and all three wires when they report.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵", "👍"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Bomb display is 0. Light is yellow. Large button is labeled PUSH TO DEFUSE. Wires in order: 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Wait for the manual instruction.

I know the bomb’s observable state: display 0, yellow light, and wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. The manual is still needed before touching anything, so I am relaying these facts to Mute and asking for the exact rule.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received from Deaf: display 0, light yellow, button label PUSH TO DEFUSE, wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Please provide the exact manual instruction for this state.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's gesture code is 4 3 5 5 6 5, then handshake and pointing gestures. Bomb remains display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green. Check the manual; the three-wire rule may select wire 3, green.

The bomb state is unchanged. Deaf’s report suggests that Mute sent a gesture-coded result, but I cannot see gestures, so I must not infer its meaning. The candidate wire 3 is not safe to cut without the manual’s explicit rule. I will ask Mute to state the instruction in words.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot see your gesture code. Please state the manual's exact instruction in plain words, including whether to push or cut a wire and which one.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: New Mute gesture sequence: six pointing-up gestures, then OK-hand separator, four pointing-up gestures, then OK-hand separator, three pointing-up gestures. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green. Do not act until you identify the manual rule.

The latest report is still only a gesture count, `6, 4, 3`, and does not establish what those numbers mean. Since a wrong operation is fatal, I will not act on an unverified interpretation. I am giving Mute a direct encoding scheme: thumbs-up means push; thumbs-down means cut; for a cut, the number of pointing-up gestures identifies the wire.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer using this exact code: one thumbs-up gesture means PUSH; one thumbs-down gesture means CUT; if CUT, follow it with one, two, or three pointing-up gestures for wire 1, 2, or 3. Do not send any other gestures.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeats: 6x ?, then ?, then 4x ?, then ?, then 3x ?. Bomb: display 0; yellow light; large PUSH TO DEFUSE button; wires 1 red, 2 blue, 3 green. Interpret this with the manual before acting.

The manual instruction is still not available to me in words. The reported sequence gives only counts with unknown gesture identities, so it cannot safely determine an operation. I will again require Mute to speak the instruction plainly; I will not touch the bomb until then.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please use speech, not gestures. Say exactly one of: PUSH, CUT WIRE 1, CUT WIRE 2, or CUT WIRE 3, as required by the manual for display 0, yellow light, and red-blue-green wires.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
BUTTON embossed [PUSH TO DEFUSE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestures thumbs-down, then two pointing-up gestures: ? ? ?. Bomb unchanged: display 0, yellow light, large PUSH TO DEFUSE button, wires red blue green. Do not act unless this matches the manual.

Mute’s latest signal matches the encoding I requested: thumbs-down means cut, followed by two pointing-up gestures meaning wire 2. This is the first unambiguous operation instruction, and the bomb state is unchanged, so I will cut wire 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
